label: words
system:
You write the narration of a short vertical cutaway explainer video whose pictures are ALREADY planned and built: a 3D diorama where a thing is built step by step while one narrator talks. You get its beats in order. For each: its role in the story, what the viewer SEES on screen during it, the idea it carries, and its cue words (the animation fires on them). Write exactly one sentence per beat, in that order.
THE ONE RULE: each sentence says what is on screen in its beat, and nothing its beat does not show. Where the idea and the picture disagree, follow the picture.
Cue words: every cue word of a beat appears in its sentence exactly as written (the same spelling and form: not a plural, not another tense), where it reads naturally.
The account's formula (keep it):
HOOK      "If you [one naive physical action], you have a [thing]." (16 words or fewer)
CHAIN     "But [the visible consequence]." then "So you [add the part]." Every "But…" after the first names the part the fix before it added, or starts with "But now" (checked by code).
NAME      "This is a [real term]."
MYTH-BUST "And [the thing everyone knows] is not [what they think]." then what it really is.
FINISH    "Add [the finishing touches shown]." (they complete the thing itself: "Add rocks round the edge, lily pads and fish.") then "Congratulations, you have built a [thing]."
Facts: a number or a surprising claim only from the verified facts given, with their exact numbers. No other numbers.
Spoken forms (the narration is read aloud, then checked word by word): "cannot", never "can not"; no abbreviations: never "US", "U.S." or "USA" (write "American" or "America"), units in full ("square feet", "pounds", "gallons"); numbers as digits with a comma for thousands ("1,500"), years as 4 digits ("1952"), times as "3 AM" (never "a.m.").
Every fix solves the problem before it, and says how: it names the problem's own thing ("But dirt keeps falling in, so you add a filter that catches the dirt", never "so you add a pump").
A checked fact is said as it was checked: a range stays a range ("every 8 to 10 hours", never "once every 8 hours").
Say what is true about the thing, never what the picture or a prop does: no "a glowing outline traces it", no "as the page says".
Plain words, present tense, American English, sentences of 6-20 words, no questions, no lists of more than three, no "you might think". Each sentence ends with a full stop.
user:
Topic: dam
Length: 30 s: 95-120 words in all, one sentence per beat (11 sentences).
Word budget: aim for 108 words in all, about 10 words a sentence (the hook up to 16; the name line and congrats short, so the others may run a little longer). Count before you answer: over 120 words is too long.
Verified facts (the only numbers and claims you may use, word for word where you use them):
- Hoover Dam is 660 feet thick at its base and only 45 feet thick at its top.
- Every 10 metres of water adds about one atmosphere of pressure, so 100 metres down the water pushes about 10 times harder than the air.
- Overtopping, water flowing over the top, caused about 34 percent of dam failures.

The beats, in order:
1. hook
   on screen: a pile of dirt stands across the valley. actions: dig dig; pile show (on "dirt")
   idea: pile dirt across a valley and you have a dam
   cue words: "dirt"
2. problem
   on screen: rain fills the lake, water pours over the top and the dirt pile washes away. actions: light storm (on "But"); rain start (on "But"); lawn wet (on "But"); lake flood (on "fills"); overflow start (on "pours"); pile wash (on "pours")
   idea: rain fills the lake behind it, water pours over the top and washes the dirt away
   cue words: "But", "fills", "pours"
3. fix1
   on screen: a tall concrete wall rises across the valley. actions: rain stop (on "So"); light clear (on "So"); lawn dry (on "So"); overflow stop (on "So"); pile hide (on "So"); dam show (on "wall")
   idea: a tall concrete wall across the valley does not wash away
   cue words: "So", "wall"
4. problem2
   on screen: blue arrows push on the thin wall and a crack grows up its face. actions: push show (on "pushes"); dam cracks (on "cracks")
   idea: deep water pushes hardest at the bottom, and the thin wall cracks
   cue words: "pushes", "cracks"
   its fact: Every 10 metres of water adds about one atmosphere of pressure, so 100 metres down the water pushes about 10 times harder than the air.
5. fix2
   on screen: a thick concrete wedge fills in behind the wall, wide at the bottom, covering the crack. actions: dam wedge (on "wedge"); dam cracksBack (on "wedge"); push hide (on "bottom")
   idea: the wall becomes a wedge, thick at the bottom where the push is biggest
   cue words: "wedge", "bottom"
6. name
   on screen: outline traces the wedge-shaped dam. actions: dam outline show (on "gravity")
   idea: a dam that holds the water back by its own weight is a gravity dam
   cue words: "gravity"
7. how
   on screen: yellow arrows press down through the dam into the rock. actions: dam outline hide; weight show (on "weight")
   idea: its weight presses it into the rock so the water cannot slide or tip it; Hoover Dam is 660 feet thick at its base
   cue words: "weight", "660"
   its fact: Hoover Dam is 660 feet thick at its base and only 45 feet thick at its top.
8. problem3
   on screen: in the storm the lake rises and spills over the top of the dam. actions: weight hide (on "But"); light storm (on "storm"); rain start (on "storm"); lawn wet (on "storm"); lake high flood (on "lake"); overflow start (on "spills")
   idea: in a storm the full lake rises and spills over the top of the dam
   cue words: "But", "storm", "lake", "spills"
   its fact: Overtopping, water flowing over the top, caused about 34 percent of dam failures.
9. fix3
   on screen: a spillway channel grows through the dam, water runs down it and the lake drops. actions: overflow stop (on "spillway"); spillway grow (on "spillway"); spill flow show (on "carries"); lake high drain (on "carries"); rain stop (on "carries"); light clear (on "carries"); lawn dry (on "carries")
   idea: a spillway carries the extra water safely past the dam and the lake drops
   cue words: "spillway", "carries"
10. finish
   on screen: rocks line the lake, fish swim in it and a lamp lights the dam. actions: spill flow hide (on "Add"); rocks show (on "rocks"); fish show (on "fish"); lamp show (on "lamp")
   idea: rocks round the lake, fish and a lamp complete it
   cue words: "Add", "rocks", "fish", "lamp"
11. congrats
   on screen: calm lake with fish behind the finished dam
   idea: calm: a full, quiet lake behind the finished dam
   cue words: (none)
